# study-planner-mcp

> Study planner MCP server. Give it your exam dates and the hours you study, the same on every day or different for each weekday, and it builds an exam schedule, a study timetable with spaced repetition review dates, pomodoro blocks and assignment milestones, and it hands the plan back as an .ics file to import into Google Calendar or Apple Calendar. Give an exam topics with their own hours and the plan says which topic to study on each day. It also answers what to study today, with the study sessions for that day, the topic of each one and the reviews that are due. Ask whether you are on track for an exam and it counts the days and study days left. Runs offline, no account. Free and open source, works with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and other MCP clients.

## Setup
- Run with npx -y study-planner-mcp
- No environment variables, no network and no account.
- Dates can be YYYY-MM-DD like 2026-12-12, or plain text like Dec 12, next Friday or in 3 weeks. If start_date is left out it uses today's date.
- A month name without a year means the next one that has not passed yet, so Dec 12 asked for in October means 12 December of that year. A weekday means the coming one, next Friday means the Friday of the week after that, and last Friday the one before. Dates with a number for the month, like 12/12/2026, are not read, so write the month as a name.
- next_review_dates counts from the day you first studied the topic and leaves out any review on or after the exam. Give from_date to say which day to count from, so the answer is repeatable.
- Study hours go in hours_per_day for every study day, and in hours_per_weekday when a weekday has its own hours, like [{day: "mon", hours: 2}, {day: "sat", hours: 6}]. Weekdays you leave out of that list use hours_per_day, a weekday with 0 hours is a day off, and days in days_off are always left out.
- An exam can carry topics with their own hours, like exams: [{name: "Networking", date: "2026-12-10", topics: [{name: "Routing", hours_needed: 6}, {name: "Switching", hours_needed: 4}]}]. The plan then names the topic of every study day, and what_to_study_today names the topic of one day. Leave hours_needed off a topic and the hours of the exam are split evenly over the topics.
- exam_countdown counts from from_date, or today, and uses the same hours_per_day, hours_per_weekday and days_off as the plan tools, so its On track or Behind verdict matches the plan.
- reschedule_missed_days takes hours_done for each exam and rebuilds the plan from start_date, so the hours you already did stay counted when a few days were missed.
- Config file per client: Claude Desktop uses mcpServers, Cursor uses mcpServers in .cursor/mcp.json or ~/.cursor/mcp.json, VS Code Copilot uses servers in .vscode/mcp.json, and the ChatGPT desktop app takes the same mcpServers JSON as a connector.

## Tools
- build_study_plan: Build a day by day study plan for one or more exams. Give each exam date and the hours you have per day, or set different hours for each weekday with hours_per_weekday, and get dated study sessions split by urgency, with a warning when the hours do not fit. Give an exam topics with their own hours and the plan names the topic of each day. Add reviews with the day you first studied each one to show Review: entries in the plan and in the calendar. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "Plan 3 weeks of study for my 4 exams, 90 minutes a day."
- make_spaced_repetition_schedule: Make a spaced repetition schedule for a topic: every review date at expanding intervals from the day you first studied it, with any date on or after the exam marked to skip. Use next_review_dates when you want the next review date only. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "When should I review what I learned today for my exam on 2026-11-30?"
- next_review_dates: Give the date of the next review for one topic, so you get a single date instead of the whole schedule. It is the first review that is not on or after the exam and has not passed yet, counting from the day you first studied it. The answer counts the reviews that already passed. Use make_spaced_repetition_schedule when you want every review date. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "When should I review the routing I studied on 2026-11-01 for my exam on 2026-11-30?"
- plan_pomodoro_sessions: Plan pomodoro sessions for a total amount of study time: work blocks separated by short breaks, with a long break after a set number of sessions. Give start_time, like 09:00, to get clock times for each block. Example prompt: "Plan 3 hours of studying as pomodoro blocks with breaks."
- list_assignment_milestones: List dated milestones that split a big assignment from a start date to the due date, with default steps for research, outline, draft, revise and proofread. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "Break my 6 hour essay due 2026-11-20 into milestones."
- export_study_plan_ics: Turn a study plan into an .ics calendar file to import into Google Calendar or Apple Calendar. It builds the same plan as build_study_plan, with the same hours_per_weekday if you set one, and answers with the whole file, so save the answer as plan.ics and open it. Every study session becomes an all day event that shows as free, with the topics of the session in its description when the exam has topics, and every exam becomes an all day event that shows as busy unless include_exams is false. Add reviews with the day you first studied each one to add Review: all day events to the calendar. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "Export my plan for a networking exam on 2026-12-12, 6 hours, starting 2026-12-07, as an ICS file."
- what_to_study_today: Answer what to study on one day in a single call: the study sessions your plan gives for that day, with the topic of each session when the exams have topics, plus the spaced repetition reviews that are due that day or are late. Give the same exams and hours you use in build_study_plan, including hours_per_weekday, and the topics you are reviewing with the day you first studied each one. Leave date out and it uses today's date. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "What should I study today? I have a networking exam on 2026-12-12 and I studied routing on 2026-11-27."
- exam_countdown: Check whether you are on track for each exam. For every exam it gives the days left, the study days left, the hours still to study, the hours to put in on each study day and a plain On track or Behind verdict, using the same hours per day, hours per weekday and days off as the plan tools. Give from_date to count from a fixed day. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "Am I on track for my exam on 2026-12-12 if I can study 2 hours a day?"
- reschedule_missed_days: Rebuild a study plan after missed study days. Give each exam the hours you have already done and it takes those off the exam, then spreads the hours that are left over the days from start_date, using the same hours_per_day, hours_per_weekday and days_off as the plan tools. When an exam has topics, the hours done come off the topics in proportion to their hours. The answer shows the hours done and the hours left for each exam, and the repaired plan from start_date. Dates can be plain text, like Dec 12 or in 3 weeks. Example prompt: "I missed three days and did 4 hours of networking. Reschedule the rest of my study."
- Aliases: make_study_plan, spaced_repetition_dates, pomodoro_plan and assignment_milestones are older names for the tools above. They take the same arguments and give the same answers, so use the names above when you can.
- Worked examples: the section below has a prompt, a tool call and the answer for every tool.

## Worked examples
Each example gives the prompt, the tool call and the answer that comes back. Arguments that are left out keep their default values. The dates are fixed, so the answers are the same on every run. The older tool names take the same arguments and give the same answers.

### Two exams and a day off

Prompt: "I have a networking exam on 2026-12-12 and scripting on 2026-12-15. I can study 3 hours a day except Sundays. Make me a plan."

Tool call: build_study_plan

```json
{
  "exams": [
    { "name": "Networking", "date": "2026-12-12", "hours_needed": 20 },
    { "name": "Scripting", "date": "2026-12-15", "hours_needed": 16 }
  ],
  "hours_per_day": 3,
  "days_off": ["sun"],
  "start_date": "2026-11-30"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Everything fits: 2 exams, 12 study days, 36h

Exams
- Networking on 2026-12-12 sat, 20h planned
- Scripting on 2026-12-15 tue, 16h planned

Plan from 2026-11-30
- 2026-11-30 mon  Networking 2h, Scripting 1h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-01 tue  Networking 2h, Scripting 1h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-02 wed  Networking 2h, Scripting 1h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-03 thu  Networking 2h, Scripting 1h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-04 fri  Networking 1.5h, Scripting 1.5h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-05 sat  Networking 2h, Scripting 1h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-07 mon  Networking 2h, Scripting 1h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-08 tue  Networking 1.5h, Scripting 1.5h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-09 wed  Networking 2h, Scripting 1h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-10 thu  Networking 1.5h, Scripting 1.5h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-11 fri  Networking 1.5h, Scripting 1.5h  (3h total)
- 2026-12-12 sat  Scripting 3h  (3h total)

Everything fits.
```

### A date in plain words

Prompt: "I have a networking exam on Dec 12 2026 and I can study 2 hours a day. Make me a plan."

Tool call: build_study_plan

```json
{
  "exams": [{ "name": "Networking", "date": "Dec 12 2026", "hours_needed": 6 }],
  "hours_per_day": 2,
  "start_date": "2026-12-07"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Everything fits: 1 exam, 3 study days, 6h

Exams
- Networking on 2026-12-12 sat, 6h planned

Plan from 2026-12-07
- 2026-12-07 mon  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-08 tue  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-09 wed  Networking 2h  (2h total)

Everything fits.
```

### An exam with topics

Prompt: "My networking exam on 2026-12-10 covers routing, switching and security. Split the study hours over those topics and make me a plan."

Tool call: build_study_plan

```json
{
  "exams": [
    {
      "name": "Networking",
      "date": "2026-12-10",
      "topics": [
        { "name": "Routing", "hours_needed": 6 },
        { "name": "Switching", "hours_needed": 4 },
        { "name": "Security", "hours_needed": 2 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "hours_per_day": 4,
  "start_date": "2026-12-07"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Everything fits: 1 exam, 3 study days, 12h

Exams
- Networking on 2026-12-10 thu, 12h planned
  - Routing 6h planned
  - Switching 4h planned
  - Security 2h planned

Plan from 2026-12-07
- 2026-12-07 mon  Networking 4h  (4h total)
  - Networking: Routing 2h, Switching 1.5h, Security 0.5h
- 2026-12-08 tue  Networking 4h  (4h total)
  - Networking: Routing 2h, Switching 1.5h, Security 0.5h
- 2026-12-09 wed  Networking 4h  (4h total)
  - Networking: Routing 2h, Switching 1h, Security 1h

Everything fits.
```

### Different hours for each weekday

Prompt: "I study 2 hours on weekdays and 6 hours on weekends. My networking exam on 2026-12-12 needs 20 hours. Make me a plan."

Tool call: build_study_plan

```json
{
  "exams": [{ "name": "Networking", "date": "2026-12-12", "hours_needed": 20 }],
  "hours_per_weekday": [
    { "day": "mon", "hours": 2 },
    { "day": "tue", "hours": 2 },
    { "day": "wed", "hours": 2 },
    { "day": "thu", "hours": 2 },
    { "day": "fri", "hours": 2 },
    { "day": "sat", "hours": 6 },
    { "day": "sun", "hours": 6 }
  ],
  "start_date": "2026-11-30"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Everything fits: 1 exam, 7 study days, 20h

Exams
- Networking on 2026-12-12 sat, 20h planned

Plan from 2026-11-30
- 2026-11-30 mon  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-01 tue  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-02 wed  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-03 thu  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-04 fri  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-05 sat  Networking 6h  (6h total)
- 2026-12-06 sun  Networking 4h  (4h total)

Everything fits.
```

### When the hours do not fit

Prompt: "My networking exam on 2026-12-12 needs 20 hours. I can only study 2 hours a day from 2026-12-10. Make me a plan."

Tool call: build_study_plan

```json
{
  "exams": [{ "name": "Networking", "date": "2026-12-12", "hours_needed": 20 }],
  "hours_per_day": 2,
  "start_date": "2026-12-10"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Not enough time: 1 exam, 2 study days, 4h

Exams
- Networking on 2026-12-12 sat, 20h planned

Plan from 2026-12-10
- 2026-12-10 thu  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-11 fri  Networking 2h  (2h total)

Not enough time. Networking is 16h short. Add study days, raise hours per day or hours per weekday, or lower the hours needed.
```

### Review dates for a topic

Prompt: "I studied routing on 2026-11-27. When should I review it for my exam on 2026-12-12?"

Tool call: make_spaced_repetition_schedule

```json
{
  "topic": "Routing",
  "first_study_date": "2026-11-27",
  "exam_date": "2026-12-12"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Review "Routing" starting from 2026-11-27 fri
- Day 1, 2026-11-28 sat
- Day 3, 2026-11-30 mon
- Day 7, 2026-12-04 fri
- Day 14, 2026-12-11 fri
- Day 30, 2026-12-27 sun (after the exam, skip)
```

### The next review for a topic

Prompt: "I studied routing on 2026-11-27. When is the next review for my exam on 2026-12-12? Today is 2026-11-29."

Tool call: next_review_dates

```json
{
  "topic": "Routing",
  "first_study_date": "2026-11-27",
  "exam_date": "2026-12-12",
  "from_date": "2026-11-29"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Next review for "Routing": 2026-11-30 mon, the 2nd review, in 1 day.
1 review has passed.
```

### Study blocks with breaks

Prompt: "Plan 90 minutes of studying as pomodoro blocks with breaks."

Tool call: plan_pomodoro_sessions

```json
{
  "total_minutes": 90
}
```

Answer:

```text
4 work sessions
- 0-25 min, work (25 min)
- 25-30 min, short break (5 min)
- 30-55 min, work (25 min)
- 55-60 min, short break (5 min)
- 60-85 min, work (25 min)
- 85-90 min, short break (5 min)
- 90-105 min, work (15 min)

Total time with breaks is 105 minutes.
```

### Milestones for a big assignment

Prompt: "Break my 6 hour history essay due 2026-11-20 into milestones. I start on 2026-11-09."

Tool call: list_assignment_milestones

```json
{
  "title": "History essay",
  "due_date": "2026-11-20",
  "estimated_hours": 6,
  "start_date": "2026-11-09"
}
```

Answer:

```text
History essay, due 2026-11-20 fri, about 6h of work
- Finish by 2026-11-11 wed, Research (1.5h)
- Finish by 2026-11-12 thu, Outline (0.5h)
- Finish by 2026-11-16 mon, First draft (2h)
- Finish by 2026-11-18 wed, Revise (1h)
- Finish by 2026-11-19 thu, Proofread and submit (0.5h)
```

### What to study on one day

Prompt: "What should I study on 2026-11-30? My networking exam is on 2026-12-12 and I studied routing on 2026-11-27."

Tool call: what_to_study_today

```json
{
  "date": "2026-11-30",
  "exams": [{ "name": "Networking", "date": "2026-12-12", "hours_needed": 12 }],
  "hours_per_day": 2,
  "reviews": [{ "topic": "Routing", "first_study_date": "2026-11-27" }]
}
```

Answer:

```text
Today 2026-11-30 mon

Study sessions, 2h total
- Networking 2h

Reviews due today
- Routing, 2nd review

Reviews to catch up
- Routing, 1st review, 2 days late (due 2026-11-28)

Next reviews
- Routing on 2026-12-04 fri, 3rd review

Next exam: Networking on 2026-12-12 sat, 12 days left.
```

### An exam countdown

Prompt: "Am I on track for my exam on 2026-12-05 if I can study 2 hours a day from 2026-11-30?"

Tool call: exam_countdown

```json
{
  "exams": [{ "name": "Networking", "date": "2026-12-05", "hours_needed": 20 }],
  "hours_per_day": 2,
  "from_date": "2026-11-30"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Exam countdown from 2026-11-30 mon

Networking, exam 2026-12-05 sat
- 5 days left, 5 study days left
- 20h still needed, 4h per study day
- Behind by 10h: your study days give 10h before the exam.
```

### The hours left after missed days

Prompt: "I missed three days of study and did 4 hours of networking. My exam is on 2026-12-12. Reschedule the rest from 2026-12-09 with 2 hours a day."

Tool call: reschedule_missed_days

```json
{
  "exams": [{ "name": "Networking", "date": "2026-12-12", "hours_needed": 10, "hours_done": 4 }],
  "hours_per_day": 2,
  "start_date": "2026-12-09"
}
```

Answer:

```text
Exams
- Networking on 2026-12-12 sat, 4h done, 6h left

Rescheduled from 2026-12-09
- 2026-12-09 wed  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-10 thu  Networking 2h  (2h total)
- 2026-12-11 fri  Networking 2h  (2h total)

Everything fits.
```

### A calendar file

Prompt: "Export my plan for a networking exam on 2026-12-12, 6 hours, starting 2026-12-07, as an ICS file."

Tool call: export_study_plan_ics

```json
{
  "exams": [{ "name": "Networking", "date": "2026-12-12", "hours_needed": 6 }],
  "hours_per_day": 2,
  "days_off": ["sun"],
  "start_date": "2026-12-07"
}
```

Answer: the whole .ics file. These are its first lines, and two more study events and one exam event follow in the same shape. DTSTAMP is the moment of the export, so yours will differ.

```text
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
VERSION:2.0
PRODID:-//AnonymousOnyx22//Study Planner MCP//EN
CALSCALE:GREGORIAN
METHOD:PUBLISH
X-WR-CALNAME:Study plan
BEGIN:VEVENT
UID:2026-12-07-networking-study@study-planner-mcp
DTSTAMP:20261021T113158Z
DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261207
DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20261208
SUMMARY:Study: Networking 2h
DESCRIPTION:Networking\, 2h of study. Day total 2h. Exam on 2026-12-12 sat.
TRANSP:TRANSPARENT
END:VEVENT
```
